issues.display_title: Issue #1820: Fix Undefined Array Key "fr" in Tour Template Processing
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Investigate the PHP/backend error Undefined array key "fr" triggered when user Vincent (#4105, vincent@timeprod.tv) applies the "Festival" template to the "Musilac" tour.

Fix Summary (Commit b7efd1f1)

The GET /templates/menu/match API experienced two main issues causing crashes (Error 409) and missing sub-menus when rendering overlay.json with grouped containers or partial localizations.

1. Undefined Array Key (409 Crash)

  • Cause: When a menu node in the JSON lacked a translation for the active language (e.g., "fr"), the parser executed $pano['name'][$lang] immediately. This triggered a fatal PHP undefined array key error caught as 409.
  • Fix: Added null coalescing ?? string structures in OverlaysClass.php. If the active language is missing, it now falls back to English ('en'), then defaults to an empty string.

2. Missing Nested Sub-Menus

  • Cause: Parent menus/categories (like "STAFF" or "SCENES") are often just label containers with no designated panoramas (id = 0). The previous loop filter $validIds completely stripped them because ID 0 was not found in the panoramas DB table. As a result, all inner sub-children nested inside were discarded alongside their parent container.
  • Fix: Expanded the filter rule in GetMatch.php. The parser will now preserve a menu node if:
    • It functions purely as a structural folder logic (has no id) OR
    • It contains child menus arrays inside its sub property OR
    • Its ID is officially a match in the DB loop.

Note: Upcoming API V2 Requirement
During debugging, we encountered menus with a multi-level nested structure (more than 1 dimension deep: i.e. sub > sub > sub).
The current parser logic still flattens the child elements down to a 1D sub array to prevent production crashes on the current frontend implementation. We plan to introduce a V2 of the endpoint to handle fully recursive JSON payloads natively without breaking legacy frontend apps that do not expect deeply nested structures.

issues.display_title: Issue #1822: Investigate and Fix Missing overlay_audit Logging on Tour Unlock
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

When user 56125 completed payment to unlock a virtual tour, a receipt PDF was generated and saved (receipt_3UBPgU4UXotNjjkl03M0nWLq_2026-09-03 01-43-23.pdf), but no record was written to the overlay_audit table. Investigate the post-payment handler to fix the root cause preventing audit entries from being inserted.

https://gothru.co/moderation/56125/receipt/receipt_3UBPgU4UXotNjjkI03M0nWLq_2026-09-03%2001-43-23.pdf

Research Notes & Hypothesis (Sept 4, 2026)

We investigated the missing overlay_audit issue using user 56125's exact transaction data. Currently, this is strictly a hypothesis because all recent testing transactions processed flawlessly as expected.

However, we identified several vulnerabilities that could lead to this edge case:

  1. Split-Brain Transactions (MyISAM vs InnoDB): Payment tracking tables (cc_logs, cc_purchase, tours) run on MyISAM (no rollback support), while overlay_audit runs on InnoDB (supports rollbacks). If the audit insert fails silently, the payment records remain permanently while the audit completely rolls back.
  2. Bypassed UPDATE Query (user_id Missing Filter): The system verifies existing audits using ONLY tour_key. If a shared/transferred tour already has an audit from a previous user, the script attempts an UPDATE instead of INSERT. Since the UPDATE is strictly filtered by user_id, 0 rows are modified without throwing any error.
  3. ENUM Implicit Mapping (1 vs 1_years): The period variable passes 1, taking advantage of MySQL's non-strict mode to implicitly map to the 1_years ENUM. An unexpected strict-mode trigger would kill the insert instantly.

Next Steps Taken:
Because we cannot currently replicate the exact failure, we have added strict, granular logging to Redis (payment:overlay-audit-debug) surrounding the ToursClass::unlockOverlayV1() mechanics. Once/if this error replicates in production, the logs will capture the exact behavior enabling us to deploy a permanent fix.
